monday-01: It's Monday morning, and Alex has a release due at six. He starts the big test migration on his laptop, and lets the agent get going.
monday-02: Halfway through, one of his Claude accounts hits its limit. Joint Bob moves the task to the next account in his pool, and the agent doesn't miss a step.
monday-03: Then an agent cleaning up old exports tries to delete customer files. Guardian stops it and asks him first, so he blocks it, and the agent archives them instead.
monday-04: Something looks off at checkout, so he asks for a dashboard, and a minute later he's looking at the errors, hour by hour.
monday-05: At lunch, his assistant tells him how the fix is going, and from his phone, he schedules the launch for six.
monday-06: Meanwhile his teammate Maya opens his conversation from her own machine, adds a request, and forks it to try a fix of her own.
monday-07: Before the review, two hosts walk him through the whole change, so he knows exactly what he's approving.
monday-08: At five forty, he moves the work to his home server, and closes the laptop. The agent keeps going.
monday-09: On the train home it finishes, and he merges the pull request from his phone.
monday-10: At six, the launch he scheduled goes out by itself, right on time.
monday-11: Joint Bob. Ship faster, and stay in charge.
lid-01: Some tasks take longer than you can stay at your desk. This one, a migration of two hundred test files, will take about forty minutes.
lid-02: So before he leaves, Alex moves it to his home server. He picks the server in Runs on, and takes ownership there, with the whole conversation and its history.
lid-03: Now he can close the laptop. The agent doesn't notice. It keeps working on the server.
lid-04: On the way home, the same conversation is on his phone, live, so he can watch it finish and open the pull request.
lid-05: And when it's done, he tells it what to do next, right from his phone.
lid-06: Joint Bob. Start anywhere. Finish anywhere.
team-01: Joint Bob works for teams too. To start one, you create a cluster in Settings, and generate an invite link that works once and expires after fifteen minutes.
team-02: Your teammate pastes the link on her own machine, and joins the cluster.
team-03: Joining doesn't share anything by itself. You choose exactly which projects your team can see, and nothing else leaves your machine.
team-04: Once a project is shared, your teammate sees its conversations live, and can write into them. Her message is answered right there, in the same conversation.
team-05: Or she can fork a conversation to try an idea of her own, while yours stays exactly as it was.
team-06: Joint Bob. Your whole team, in the same conversation.
pools-01: If your team pays for several Claude accounts, Joint Bob can use all of them. You add each one in Settings, under Connections, as a profile that you sign in to once.
pools-02: Next, you create a pool. You give it a name, and list the accounts in the order they should be tried: account one first, then two, then three.
pools-03: Then you choose where the pool applies. It can be your default for everything, or cover one workspace, one project, a single conversation, or your whole team.
pools-04: Now, when an account reaches its limit, the turn moves to the next one in the pool before the reply starts. When that one runs out too, the third takes over, and the agent carries on.
pools-05: Joint Bob. Use everything you already pay for.
budgets-01: Agents can run for hours, so Joint Bob lets you put a ceiling on what they spend. If you manage a team, you set limits for everyone under Settings, Cluster, Budget.
budgets-02: Any project or conversation can also get a tighter limit of its own, by the hour, day, week, month or in total, from the Budget option in its menu.
budgets-03: As spending gets close, at eighty percent of a limit, a notice appears above the message box, showing how much has been used, and of which limit.
budgets-04: And once a limit is reached, Joint Bob doesn't start any new work until it resets or you raise it, so there are no surprise bills.
budgets-05: Joint Bob. Your agents, on a budget.
guardian-01: Guardian is a set of rules that every agent has to follow. Each rule is a plain yes or no question, such as: is this command dangerous?
guardian-02: Once you switch it on in Settings, Guardian checks every command, every file change, and everything an agent is about to send to the model.
guardian-03: When an action matches a rule, the agent is paused, and you're asked first. Here, an agent wants to delete twelve hundred customer files.
guardian-04: You click Block, and the agent is told why. So it finds a safer way, and archives the files instead of deleting them.
guardian-05: And if you paste a key into a message by mistake, Guardian removes it before the message ever reaches the model.
guardian-06: Joint Bob. Your rules, on every agent.
story-01: Reviewing a change means working out what was done, and why. Story mode writes that up for you, straight from the conversation that made it.
story-02: You get a clear account of what changed and the reasons behind it, worked examples of the new behavior, and the parts of the code that matter.
story-03: Or press Overview, and two hosts talk you through the change as a short show, in voices that run on your own machine.
story-04: If something isn't clear, ask a question, and the answer is added to the show as a new chapter.
story-05: Joint Bob. Review the story, not just the diff.
dashboards-01: Every project can have its own dashboards, and you don't have to build them yourself. You just describe what you want to see.
dashboards-02: A dashboard agent then explores where the data lives, builds the page, and writes a small script that knows how to refresh it.
dashboards-03: You check the draft, and save it. Its charts, headline numbers and tables run in a sandbox, with no access to the network.
dashboards-04: From then on, Refresh simply runs that script, so new numbers arrive in seconds, without another call to the AI.
dashboards-05: Joint Bob. Ask for a dashboard. Get one.
phone-01: Joint Bob runs on your own machines, and your phone can reach them too. You open it in the phone's browser, and install it, like any other app.
phone-02: All of your projects and conversations are there, including the ones running on your home server right now.
phone-03: Open one, and you pick it up exactly where it was, with its full history and the agent's progress.
phone-04: Then you type the next step and send it. The work carries on on the server, and you follow along from wherever you are.
phone-05: Joint Bob. Your desk, in your pocket.
schedule-01: Some checks need doing every hour, and nobody wants to do them. A scheduled task hands that job to an agent.
schedule-02: You open a project's scheduled tasks, write what the agent should look for, and choose how often it runs, on which machine, and with which agent.
schedule-03: From then on, it runs by itself. Every hour, a new conversation starts, and the agent reviews that hour's support calls.
schedule-04: When it finds a problem, it traces the cause, fixes it, and opens a pull request, then writes up what it did.
schedule-05: The report waits in your review inbox, so all you have to do is read it.
schedule-06: Joint Bob. Set it once. It keeps watching.
alerts-01: A webhook is a private address that starts work in Joint Bob. You create one in Settings, choose the project, and write standing instructions for the agent.
alerts-02: Then you point your alerting tool at it. When production breaks at three in the morning, the alert calls the webhook, and a new conversation begins.
alerts-03: The agent reads the alert, finds the bug, fixes it and opens a pull request, with nobody at a keyboard.
alerts-04: In the morning, the report and the fix are waiting in your inbox.
alerts-05: Joint Bob. Alerts that fix themselves.
browser-01: Some bugs only show up in a real browser. In Joint Bob, the agent gets one, right inside the conversation.
browser-02: It clicks through your site the way a customer would. Here, it adds a mug to the cart, and tries a promo code at checkout.
browser-03: It sees the error for itself, reads the code to find the cause, fixes it, and then goes back to check that the order goes through.
browser-04: You can watch every step live, and if you need to, take control of the browser yourself, then hand it back to the agent.
browser-05: Joint Bob. Give your agent a real browser.
secrets-01: Agents often need keys and tokens. In Joint Bob, you add each one once, as a secret account, and it's stored encrypted.
secrets-02: Your other machines receive it automatically, so the same account works wherever the conversation runs.
secrets-03: You can share it with your team as well. Teammates can use it, but only you can change it.
secrets-04: Attach it to a workspace, a project or a single conversation, and agents there can use it without asking you for it.
secrets-05: The key is in the agent's environment, so it never has to be pasted into the chat.
secrets-06: Joint Bob. One place for your keys.
analytics-01: Joint Bob keeps track of what every conversation costs. The Costs view shows where the money went, by project, model, label and skill.
analytics-02: Compare one period with another, and it tells you what changed, and which projects or models made the difference.
analytics-03: It also shows which skills cost the most, and which ones fail more often than the rest, so you know what to fix first.
analytics-04: Joint Bob. Know what your agents cost. And why.
assistant-01: Any conversation can become an assistant: an agent with a name, its own instructions, and one chat that you can open on your laptop or your phone.
assistant-02: You tell it what to look after. Alex's release assistant keeps track of the checkout work, his meetings, and his launches.
assistant-03: Ask how a feature is going, and it answers from the work in your project's conversations: what's merged, what's left, and what's in the way.
assistant-04: With your calendar connected, it books meetings too, like a review with Maya tomorrow at ten.
assistant-05: Most importantly, it schedules launches. From his phone, Alex sets one for every Monday at six, with the steps the release should follow.
assistant-06: At six, the launch runs through the assistant on its own, and the report lands in the same chat.
assistant-07: Joint Bob. Your launches, on schedule.
short-01: Alex has a release due at six. His agents start on it at nine.
short-02: When one Claude account runs out, the next one in his pool takes over.
short-03: Guardian asks him before anything risky, and his assistant schedules the launch.
short-04: At five forty, he moves the work to his server, and merges from the train.
short-05: At six, the launch goes out, on time.
